910.name: Prehistoric Malay Peninsula and Borneo
910.description: The earliest human habitation in the Malay Peninsula and Sabah/Sarawak, the Niah Cave discoveries in Borneo, Austronesian migrations, and the Orang Asli as the indigenous peoples.

sub_clusters.name: Niah Cave and Early Habitation
sub_clusters.description: The Niah Cave archaeological site in Sarawak with some of the earliest evidence of human habitation in Southeast Asia, Hoabinhian culture, and the indigenous peoples of the peninsula.
key_events: Niah Cave skull — one of the oldest anatomically modern human remains in Southeast Asia (c. 40,000 years ago)

sub_clusters.name: Austronesian Settlement and Metal Age
sub_clusters.description: Austronesian migrations into the peninsula and Borneo, the development of coastal trading communities, bronze and iron working, and early contacts with Indian maritime traders.

910.name: Early Indianized States
910.description: The emergence of Indianized trading polities on the Malay Peninsula — Langkasuka, Kedah (Kadaram), Chi Tu, and Pan Pan — serving as entrepôts on the maritime Silk Road.

sub_clusters.name: Langkasuka and Kedah
sub_clusters.description: The Hindu-Buddhist kingdoms of Langkasuka in the northern peninsula and the Bujang Valley civilization in Kedah, their role in Indian Ocean trade, and Chinese diplomatic records of these polities.
key_events: Bujang Valley temples in Kedah — earliest Hindu-Buddhist archaeological remains in Malaysia (c. 4th–5th century AD)

920.name: Srivijaya and the Malay Peninsula
920.description: Srivijayan suzerainty over the Malay Peninsula, the Chola raids, the Siamese southward expansion, and the emergence of small Malay trading ports that would coalesce into Malacca.

sub_clusters.name: Srivijayan Period
sub_clusters.description: The Malay Peninsula under Srivijayan influence and later control, the Chola raids on Kedah, the Ligor inscription, and the gradual weakening of Srivijayan hegemony.

sub_clusters.name: Post-Srivijaya Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: The decline of Srivijaya, Siamese expansion into the northern Malay states, the Majapahit claim over the peninsula, Temasek (Singapore), and the founding conditions for Malacca.

930.name: Sultanate of Malacca
930.description: The founding of Malacca by Parameswara, its conversion to Islam, its rise as the greatest entrepôt in Southeast Asia, and the creation of the Malay-Islamic cultural paradigm that defines modern Malaysia.

sub_clusters.name: Founding and Islamization
sub_clusters.description: Parameswara's flight from Palembang and founding of Malacca, his conversion to Islam, the alliance with Ming China, Zheng He's visits, and the Sultanate's rapid commercial growth.
key_events: Parameswara founds Malacca at the strategic straits (c. 1400)
Zheng He's treasure fleet visits Malacca, establishing Ming protection (1405–1433)

sub_clusters.name: Golden Age and Portuguese Conquest
sub_clusters.description: Malacca's zenith as the greatest trading port in Southeast Asia under Sultan Mansur Shah and the Bendahara Tun Perak, the Malay legal code (Undang-undang Melaka), and the Portuguese conquest by Afonso de Albuquerque.
key_events: Malacca becomes the premier entrepôt of Southeast Asia with over 100 languages spoken in its markets
Afonso de Albuquerque conquers Malacca for Portugal (1511)

930.name: Successor Sultanates and European Rivalry
930.description: The Malay successor sultanates of Johor, Perak, and Aceh vying to inherit Malacca's legacy, Portuguese and then Dutch control of Malacca, and the British entry into the Malay world.

sub_clusters.name: Johor Sultanate and Portuguese-Dutch Era
sub_clusters.description: The Johor Sultanate as successor to Malacca, the triangular rivalry with Portugal and Aceh, the Dutch capture of Malacca in 1641, and the Johor-Riau empire's golden age.
key_events: Dutch capture Malacca from the Portuguese with Johor's help (1641)

sub_clusters.name: Bugis Influence and British Arrival
sub_clusters.description: Bugis warrior-traders dominating Johor and Selangor, Francis Light's founding of Penang, Raffles' founding of Singapore, and the Anglo-Dutch Treaty dividing the Malay world.
key_events: Francis Light founds Penang as the first British settlement in Malaya (1786)
Anglo-Dutch Treaty of 1824 divides the Malay world between British and Dutch spheres

940.name: British Malaya
940.description: The Straits Settlements, the Residential System in the Malay States, tin and rubber boom, mass immigration of Chinese and Indian laborers, and the formation of the multiethnic society.

sub_clusters.name: Straits Settlements and Residential System
sub_clusters.description: The Straits Settlements of Penang, Malacca, and Singapore, the Pangkor Treaty and introduction of British Residents, the tin mining boom, and the beginnings of mass Chinese and Indian immigration.
key_events: Pangkor Treaty — British impose the Residential System on Perak (1874)
Formation of the Federated Malay States (Perak, Selangor, Negeri Sembilan, Pahang) (1895)

sub_clusters.name: Rubber Boom and Colonial Society
sub_clusters.description: The rubber plantation economy, massive Indian labor migration, Chinese tin miners and merchants, the Unfederated Malay States, the founding of UMNO nationalism, and the approach of war.
key_events: Rubber becomes Malaya's dominant export, transforming the economy and demographics (early 1900s)

950.name: Japanese Occupation and Malayan Emergency
950.description: The Japanese conquest and brutal occupation, the post-war Malayan Union controversy, the Malayan Emergency anti-communist campaign, and the achievement of Merdeka (independence).

sub_clusters.name: Japanese Occupation and Resistance
sub_clusters.description: The rapid Japanese conquest of Malaya, the fall of Singapore, the Sook Ching massacre of ethnic Chinese, the communist MPAJA resistance, and the war's lasting impact on inter-ethnic relations.
key_events: Japanese forces conquer Malaya and capture Singapore (February 1942)
Sook Ching massacre — systematic killing of ethnic Chinese in Malaya and Singapore (1942)

sub_clusters.name: Malayan Union Controversy and Merdeka
sub_clusters.description: The failed Malayan Union proposal, the formation of UMNO, the Malayan Emergency (1948–1960), Tunku Abdul Rahman's Alliance coalition, and the achievement of independence.
key_events: Malaya achieves independence (Merdeka) under Tunku Abdul Rahman (31 August 1957)

sub_clusters.name: Malayan Emergency
sub_clusters.description: The communist insurgency by the MCP/MRLA, the British counterinsurgency campaign, the Briggs Plan resettlement, the assassination of Sir Henry Gurney, and the eventual defeat of the insurgents.

960.name: Formation of Malaysia and Konfrontasi
960.description: The creation of the Federation of Malaysia incorporating Sabah and Sarawak, Indonesian Konfrontasi, the expulsion of Singapore, and the traumatic May 13 racial riots.

sub_clusters.name: Malaysia Formation and Singapore Separation
sub_clusters.description: Tunku Abdul Rahman's Malaysia proposal, the incorporation of Sabah, Sarawak, and Singapore, Indonesian Konfrontasi, Philippine claims, and Singapore's expulsion from the federation.
key_events: Federation of Malaysia formed incorporating Malaya, Singapore, Sabah, and Sarawak (16 September 1963)
Singapore expelled from Malaysia (9 August 1965)

sub_clusters.name: May 13 Incident and New Economic Policy
sub_clusters.description: The May 13 racial riots in Kuala Lumpur, the declaration of emergency, the Rukunegara national principles, and the launch of the New Economic Policy to restructure society.
key_events: May 13 racial riots in Kuala Lumpur trigger fundamental policy restructuring (13 May 1969)

960.name: Mahathir Era and Modernization
960.description: Mahathir Mohamad's transformative 22-year premiership, rapid industrialization, the Petronas Twin Towers, Look East policy, the Anwar Ibrahim crisis, and the Asian financial crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Industrialization and Vision 2020
sub_clusters.description: Mahathir's Look East policy, heavy industrialization (Proton car), the Multimedia Super Corridor, the Petronas Twin Towers, and Vision 2020 to achieve developed-nation status.
key_events: Petronas Twin Towers completed — world's tallest buildings (1998)
Proton Saga launched as Malaysia's first national car (1985)

sub_clusters.name: Asian Financial Crisis and Anwar Affair
sub_clusters.description: The 1997 Asian financial crisis, Mahathir's unorthodox capital controls, the sacking and imprisonment of Deputy PM Anwar Ibrahim, the Reformasi movement, and Mahathir's retirement in 2003.
key_events: Mahathir imposes capital controls defying IMF orthodoxy during the Asian crisis (1998)
Anwar Ibrahim sacked and arrested, sparking the Reformasi movement (1998)

960.name: Contemporary Malaysia
960.description: The post-Mahathir era, the 1MDB scandal, the historic 2018 election defeat of UMNO/BN, Mahathir's return, political instability, the Sheraton Move, and the unity government.

sub_clusters.name: 1MDB Scandal and 2018 Election
sub_clusters.description: The massive 1MDB sovereign wealth fund scandal under PM Najib Razak, the historic 2018 election defeat of UMNO/BN after 61 years, Mahathir's return as PM, and the Sheraton Move political crisis.
key_events: Pakatan Harapan defeats UMNO/BN in historic election; 92-year-old Mahathir returns as PM (May 2018)
Sheraton Move political crisis topples the elected government (February 2020)

sub_clusters.name: Unity Government and Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Political instability under Muhyiddin and Ismail Sabri, the 2022 election producing a hung parliament, Anwar Ibrahim finally becoming PM at age 75, and the unity government's reform agenda.
key_events: Anwar Ibrahim becomes Prime Minister after decades of struggle (November 2022)
Najib Razak convicted and imprisoned for 1MDB corruption (2022)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
